 Netflix is showing a drama so gripping viewers binge 'for 7 hours straight'
 "We started episode 1 at 8pm and next thing we knew it was 3am."
 Add to preferred sources Comments TV Ketsuda Phoutinane Spare Time Content Editor 11:49, 08 Nov 2026 View 2 Images (Image: USA/Netflix) 
 We've all experienced it; scrolling through Netflix , iPlayer and back again hoping to stumble upon something good to watch. A new release might grab your attention, but occasionally all it requires is a personal recommendation to guide you towards your next binge watch .
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 A dark Netflix show is neither recent nor particularly well-known, but audiences are captivated by the "electrifying" crime drama . Fans have confessed to calling off plans, remaining awake until the early hours, and squandering an entire summer's day indoors to keep watching.
 ‌ 
 The Sinner is about the disturbing murder of a man stabbed to death by a young mother. Initially conceived as a miniseries, the show proved so popular it went on for three more series.
 ‌ 
 What is The Sinner about?
 Bill Pullman portrays a detective attempting to understand what drove a young mum, Cora Tannetti ( Jessica Biel ), to brutally murder a stranger.
 The thriller boasts an impressive 92% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with following series scoring between 88% and 92%. The critics' consensus says: "The Sinner's first season, as a standalone, is as good as it gets. If you're looking for a murder mystery to sustain your dark impulses and drag you kicking and screaming from start to finish, look no further."
 View 2 Images Netflix (Image: Netflix) 
 ‌ 
 The series, which ran from 2017 to 2021 on the USA Network, was based on the novel of the same name by Petra Hammesfahr. It evolved into an anthology format, with the detective tackling a different murder case each season.
 The synopsis of The Sinner reads: "Detective Harry Ambrose investigates various atrocious murder cases and tries to analyse the reasons behind ordinary people committing heinous crimes.
 ‌ 
 "He employs some unusual tactics and a deep capacity for empathy to solve his cases. His boundless dedication is driven by his dark past, leading him into powerful and often dangerously intimate bonds with his suspects."

 ‌ 
 What audiences say
 The Sinner came highly recommended when a Reddit user requested something "impossible to pause". They said: "Which TV series had you saying 'just one more episode'... until it was suddenly 3am?".
 "I'm looking for shows with that binge effect - the ones that hook you so hard, it's impossible to stop at just one episode. I want twists, cliffhangers, intense pacing - anything that makes you lose all track of time.
 ‌ 
 "Not necessarily the most famous or critically acclaimed, just the most impossible to pause. You know the kind. What are the shows that grabbed you by the throat and wouldn't let go? !"
 One person said: "Had plans to go out with a roommate. We started episode 1 at 8pm and next thing we knew it was 3am". To which another replied: "Literally the first show I thought of!"
 ‌ 
 The feeling was echoed by a film critic: "After one episode, you'll happily want to skip the beach to stay home and watch the show you can't help but become obsessed with."
 An IMDB user declared: "This show is the BEST THRILLER to come out in a long time. It's the type of show where you are always inside the screen. You are paying close attention to every little detail, you are trying to connect all the dots, you want to untangle the characters, get in their mind, solve the mystery and at last you will be asking 'WHY CORA TANNETTI DID THIS??'.
 ‌ 
 "The performances are top-notch; you can see inside the character through the actor. Jessica Biel really leads the show in an extraordinary manner.
 "The plot is amazing and [the] writing makes sure the show is always connected to the original content.
 Article continues below "The mystery deepens with every episode and you will be left crying for the next one. DON'T MISS IT! ! !"
 All four series of The Sinner are available to stream on Netflix UK. Membership starts from £7.99 per month.
